optical-switch shipments (fortnight:c1/c.description: Will Nvidia's co-packaged-optics (CPO) switch shipments reach volume in calendar 2027 — approaching the 30,000 units by mid-2027 and the 100,000 units for the full year that GF Securities forecasts?
optical-switch shipments (fortnight:c1/c.outcome: Nvidia's CPO switch shipment volume from Q4 2026 through calendar 2027 (GF Securities: 15,000 units in Q4 2026, 16,000 in early 2027, 30,000 by mid-2027, 100,000 for all of 2027), as reflected in Nvidia's networking revenue disclosures and suppliers' CPO/NPO laser shipments.
optical-switch shipments (fortnight:c1/c.period: Calendar 2027, with the item's stated checkpoints at Q4 2026, early 2027 and mid-2027, checked against Nvidia's quarterly results and supplier disclosures. The item gives no confirmation date, so the forecast periods it states fix the check dates.

chip sales into China (fortnight:c1/clea.description: Will Nvidia be permitted to sell its current Blackwell-generation AI chips into China — through U.S. export approval and Chinese acceptance of shipments — by the end of fiscal 2027?
chip sales into China (fortnight:c1/clea.outcome: Whether U.S. authorities extend export approval beyond the older H200 to Nvidia's current Blackwell-generation chips for approved Chinese customers, and whether Chinese authorities stop restricting Nvidia chip shipments, so that China data-center revenue can resume; the item reports H200 shipments are already U.S.-permitted while Chinese authorities still restrict them.
chip sales into China (fortnight:c1/clea.period: NVIDIA fiscal year ending late January 2027 — the current fiscal year-end, used as the check date for a pending regulatory decision per section 3 (item gives no date of its own).

an acquisition (week-10-06:c1/clean-11).description: Will Nvidia sign and complete an acquisition of Reflection AI — and at what consideration and terms — by the check date?
an acquisition (week-10-06:c1/clean-11).outcome: A definitive agreement to acquire Reflection AI, its closing (or the talks' collapse), and the final consideration paid and any regulatory conditions imposed.
an acquisition (week-10-06:c1/clean-11).period: Check date: April 2028, the outer limit of a date within 18 months of the Oct. 10, 2026 item for an acquisition not yet signed.

investment commitments (week-10-06:c1/cl.description: How much of Nvidia's $25 billion of equity-investment commitments outstanding at July 26, 2026 will be funded or remain outstanding at its next annual report?
investment commitments (week-10-06:c1/cl.outcome: The remaining balance of Nvidia's equity-investment commitments, the cash paid to fund them, and any change in the committed amounts, as disclosed in Nvidia's next annual report.
investment commitments (week-10-06:c1/cl.period: Nvidia's next annual report (fiscal year ending late January 2027), as fixed by the reason for an obligation already undertaken.

memory prices (week-10-06:c1/clean-3).description: By how much will contract prices for AI-server memory (HBM/DRAM) — the memory input cost embedded in Nvidia's GPUs — rise or fall in calendar 2027?
memory prices (week-10-06:c1/clean-3).outcome: The change in HBM/DRAM contract prices over calendar 2027, and the memory makers' reported average selling prices and memory gross margins for the periods covering 2027.
memory prices (week-10-06:c1/clean-3).period: Calendar 2027 (overlapping Micron's fiscal 2027, roughly September 2026–August 2027), as supported by Micron management's fiscal 2027 price guidance in the October 6, 2026 article.

a chip export licence (week-10-06:c1/cle.description: Will the U.S. licence requirement on Nvidia's data center chips still bar it from China's data center compute market at Nvidia's fiscal 2027 year-end, or will it be lifted before then?
a chip export licence (week-10-06:c1/cle.outcome: Whether the U.S. export-licence requirement on Nvidia's H20-class data center products remains in force or is lifted, and whether Nvidia resumes recognizing data center compute revenue from China.
a chip export licence (week-10-06:c1/cle.period: Nvidia's fiscal year ending late January 2027 (current fiscal year-end, the date fixed for the pending export-control status).

pool-9.description: How much will DRAM, NAND and high-bandwidth memory contract prices rise in calendar 2026, and what will the memory content of NVIDIA's Vera Rubin VR200 rack cost, now that memory is reported to be 25-30% of the rack bill of materials?
pool-9.outcome: The direction and size of 2026 memory contract price increases and the memory cost per NVIDIA Vera Rubin rack (Morgan Stanley currently puts memory content at about $2 million per rack, up 435%), which bears on NVIDIA's per-rack cost/ASP economics and on hyperscaler AI-infrastructure spending.
pool-9.period: Calendar year 2026 — checked against memory contract price releases and NVIDIA/partner disclosures of rack bill-of-materials as Vera Rubin ramps during H2 2026.

u1/clean-5.description: What will contract prices for AI memory (LPDDR5X, HBM, 3D NAND/DRAM) be through calendar 2026-2027 — the input that now makes up roughly 25-30% of Nvidia's Vera Rubin rack cost?
u1/clean-5.outcome: The level and direction of contract memory (DRAM, NAND, HBM) prices in 2026-2027 and the resulting per-rack memory content cost (about $2 million on the VR200).
u1/clean-5.period: Calendar 2026-2027 memory contract cycles; set by the item's forward cost period (second half of 2026 and beyond).

u3/clean-11.description: Will custom ASIC AI accelerators designed by Broadcom and Marvell take a growing share of the big four hyperscalers' AI accelerator spending in calendar 2027, at Nvidia's expense, given their lower cost per gigawatt?
u3/clean-11.outcome: The split of big-four hyperscaler 2027 AI accelerator spending (and of the 19.5 GW of incremental compute capacity projected for 2027) between custom ASIC racks and Nvidia GPU racks, measured against the item's cost-per-gigawatt estimates of $6–11 billion for Broadcom/Marvell ASIC racks versus roughly $19 billion for Nvidia GB300-based racks and $25 billion under Vera Rubin.
u3/clean-11.period: Calendar 2027 — set by the item: Morgan Stanley forecasts the big four will spend over $1 trillion on AI infrastructure 'next year' and add 19.5 GW of capacity, the period in which the ASIC-versus-GPU mix plays out.
